zipCodeComparison.areaName: Central Parsippany, Troy Hills, Powder Mill & Lake Parsippany
zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Troy Hills, Powder Mill, Parsippany Hills, Lake Parsippany, Knollwood, Rockaway Neck
keyFindings: Represents three-quarters of Parsippany's population and generates 76.8% of the residential school and municipal tax levy.
Includes both high-value custom colonials in Powder Mill/Troy Hills ($430k+ assessments) and modest bungalows around Lake Parsippany ($285k assessments).
Contains the Campus Drive, Sylvan Way, and Route 10 corporate corridors where 30-year PILOT apartment conversions are concentrated.

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Lake Hiawatha, North Beverwyck Rd Corridor, Lower Knollwood
keyFindings: Walkable downtown commercial & residential neighborhood with the highest property tax effort as a share of household income (10.75%).
Nearly 49% renter households in garden apartments and multi-family homes along North Beverwyck Road.
Supplies nearly 20% of public school students while paying 14.2% of the residential tax levy.

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Mount Tabor Historic District (Camp Meeting Grounds), Country Club Rd Enclave
keyFindings: Founded in 1869 as a Victorian Methodist camp-meeting community; listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Served by Fire District #1 and its own dedicated Mount Tabor Branch Library and NJ Transit train station border.
High homeownership rate (82%) with unique historic cottage and Victorian architecture.

zipCodeComparison.areaName: Southwest Parsippany / Greystone / Morris Plains Border
zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Littleton Rd (Rt 202) West, Greystone Park Border, Intervale / Powder Mill West
keyFindings: Affluent western section of Parsippany sharing the 07950 postal code with neighboring Morris Plains.
Carries the highest average residential assessments ($412,000) and average annual tax bills ($14,626/yr) in the township.
Feeds into Parsippany Hills High School and Brooklawn Middle School.

neighborhoods.name: Powder Mill & Parsippany Hills
neighborhoods.character: Executive Split-Levels, Center-Hall Colonials & Wooded Lots
neighborhoods.description: Located in western/southwest Parsippany near Parsippany Hills High School and Morris Plains border. Features spacious 4–5 bedroom colonials and split-levels on quarter- to half-acre lots.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Highest nominal residential tax bills in Parsippany ($14,500–$21,000/yr), acting as a major net tax donor to the school and municipal levy.

neighborhoods.name: Troy Hills & South Beverwyck
neighborhoods.character: Historic Suburban Core, Colonials, Bi-Levels & Cul-de-Sacs
neighborhoods.description: Stretching along South Beverwyck Road, Reynolds Ave, and Troy Rd toward Whippany. Home to Troy Hills Elementary and classic mid-century and modern suburban subdivisions.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Strong middle-to-upper-middle class tax base; homeowners have absorbed steep school levy increases as nearby Route 10 office parks lost assessment value.

neighborhoods.name: Lake Parsippany
neighborhoods.character: Lakefront Community, Expanded Ranches, Capes & Rebuild Colonials
neighborhoods.description: Built around the 168-acre Lake Parsippany (LPPOA) in the southern-central section of town. Mix of 1930s–1950s summer cottages converted to year-round homes and modern rebuilds.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Served by Fire District #3; residents pay both township property taxes ($11,076 avg) and optional/deeded Lake Parsippany Property Owners Association fees.

neighborhoods.name: Lake Hiawatha
neighborhoods.character: High-Density Residential, Walkable Commercial Corridor & Garden Apartments
neighborhoods.description: Northeastern section of Parsippany centered on North Beverwyck Road and Lake Shore Drive, bordering Montville and Boonton. Features local restaurants, shops, single-family capes, and apartment complexes.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Bears the highest property tax burden as a percentage of household income (10.75%) and serves as a major source of students for Lake Hiawatha Elementary, Central MS, and Parsippany High School.

neighborhoods.name: Mount Tabor & Rainbow Lakes
neighborhoods.character: Historic Victorian Camp-Meeting Enclave & Lakefront Homes
neighborhoods.description: Northwest corner of Parsippany bordering Denville. Includes the 1869 Mount Tabor Historic District with gingerbread Victorian cottages and the scenic Rainbow Lakes community.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Served by Fire Districts #1 (Mt. Tabor) and #2 (Rainbow Lakes); high civic engagement and historic preservation protections.

neighborhoods.name: Knollwood, Lake Intervale & Greystone
neighborhoods.character: North/West Commuter Subdivisions, Townhomes & Country Club Corridor
neighborhoods.description: Encompasses the northern and western corridors near Knoll Country Club, Intervale Road (Waterview), and Littleton Road (07950 border).
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Directly impacted by high-density luxury apartment and townhome redevelopments along Route 202 and Route 46.

keyTakeaways.title: 64.1% of Every Tax Dollar Goes to PTHSD Because State Aid is Under 10%
keyTakeaways.detail: Because Parsippany is classified by the State of New Jersey as a higher-wealth Morris County suburb, State Education Aid covers only 9.7% ($18.26M) of the $187.45M school budget. Local homeowners must fund 86.4% ($161.99M) of the school district.

keyTakeaways.title: The Corporate Office Park to PILOT Apartment Double-Whammy
keyTakeaways.detail: For decades, corporate campuses on Campus Drive, Sylvan Way, and Route 10 subsidized homeowners by paying taxes without sending children to school. Converting those offices into 30-year PILOT apartment complexes eliminated commercial school ratables while adding hundreds of public school students.

keyTakeaways.title: Lake Hiawatha (07034) Bears the Highest Income Strain (10.75%)
keyTakeaways.detail: While Powder Mill and 07950 pay the highest dollar tax bills ($14,626–$15,194/yr), modest single-family homes and renters in Lake Hiawatha (07034) face the highest tax burden relative to median income.
